## Singapore Weekly Grocery Plan for 3 People
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg

A practical **SGD 160** plan for **5 dinners + 3 packable work lunches** using ingredients that are easy to find at **FairPrice, Sheng Siong, Giant, Cold Storage, or wet markets**. The menu keeps meals simple, repeatable, and budget-aware.

## 5 Dinners + 3 Lunches: Budget-Friendly Meal Mix
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

| Meal | Idea | Main ingredients | Est. cost |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Dinner 1 | Chicken rice-style plate | Chicken thighs, rice, cucumber, ginger, garlic | SGD 18 |
| Dinner 2 | Vegetarian tofu veg stir-fry with rice | Firm tofu, cabbage, carrots, bok choy, mushrooms | SGD 14 |
| Dinner 3 | Fish curry with rice | White fish, curry paste/powder, potatoes, onions, tomatoes | SGD 22 |
| Dinner 4 | Minced pork or chicken bee hoon | Bee hoon, minced meat, bean sprouts, chye sim, egg | SGD 16 |
| Dinner 5 | Soy-garlic chicken noodles | Chicken, noodles, broccoli, capsicum, soy sauce | SGD 18 |
| Lunch 1 | Fried rice box | Rice, egg, mixed veg, leftover chicken | SGD 8 |
| Lunch 2 | Tuna or egg sandwich wrap | Bread/wraps, tuna or eggs, lettuce, cucumber | SGD 10 |
| Lunch 3 | Noodle salad box | Noodles, tofu or chicken, cucumber, corn, sesame dressing | SGD 10 |

Estimated meal spend: **SGD 116**
Remaining for pantry, snacks, fruit, milk, and price buffer: **SGD 44**

## Shopping List by Category
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cart.svg

### Protein
- Chicken thighs or drumsticks, about 1.5–2 kg
- White fish fillets, about 600–800 g
- Firm tofu, 3–4 blocks
- Eggs, 1 tray
- Minced pork or minced chicken, about 400–500 g
- Canned tuna, 2 cans

### Vegetables
- Cabbage, 1 head
- Carrots, 4–6
- Bok choy or chye sim, 2 bunches
- Bean sprouts, 1 pack
- Potatoes, 4–6 medium
- Onions, 3–4
- Garlic, 1 bulb
- Ginger, 1 piece
- Cucumber, 2
- Tomatoes, 3–4
- Broccoli or cauliflower, 1–2 heads
- Capsicum, 2
- Lettuce or salad mix, 1 pack
- Mushrooms, 1 pack
- Corn kernels, 1 can or frozen pack

### Carbs and Staples
- Rice, 2–3 kg
- Bee hoon, 1–2 packs
- Egg noodles or yellow noodles, 1 pack
- Bread or wraps, 1–2 packs
- Plain flour or cornstarch if needed for thickening

### Pantry and Seasoning
- Cooking oil
- Light soy sauce
- Dark soy sauce
- Oyster sauce or vegetarian stir-fry sauce
- Curry paste or curry powder
- Salt and pepper
- Sesame oil
- Sugar
- Stock cubes or broth powder
- Chili sauce or sambal

### Fruit and Extras
- Bananas, apples, or mandarins
- Milk or soy milk
- Yogurt or snacks if budget allows

## Budget Split That Fits SGD 160
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-dollar.svg

- **Protein:** SGD 60–70
- **Vegetables:** SGD 25–30
- **Carbs/staples:** SGD 20–25
- **Pantry/seasoning top-up:** SGD 15–20
- **Fruit, milk, snacks, buffer:** SGD 20–30

A good target is to keep protein slightly higher because it drives most of the meal cost, especially with fish.

## Supermarket-Friendly Meal Notes
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg

- Use **chicken thighs/drumsticks** instead of breast for better value and easier cooking.
- Choose **firm tofu, cabbage, bean sprouts, and bok choy** because they are common, affordable, and hold up well in stir-fries.
- For the fish meal, pick a **budget white fish** such as dory, batang, or local market equivalent if fresh fillets are too costly.
- Stretch meals by serving with **rice or noodles plus 2 vegetables**.
- Pack lunches from dinner leftovers where possible to reduce waste and cost.
